## Overview

For this assignment, I plan to use the New York Times Most Popular API to explore which newspaper sections appear most often among its most-viewed articles over the past seven days. I am interested in seeing which topics are most represented in that list.

I will request the data in R, convert the JSON response into a clean data frame, and count the articles in each section. These counts will describe the articles returned by the API, rather than the total number of views each section received.

## Selected API and Request

I plan to use the Most Popular API’s most-viewed endpoint:

<https://api.nytimes.com/svc/mostpopular/v2/viewed/7.json>

The `7` specifies a seven-day period. I will create an account through the New York Times Developer Portal, enable the Most Popular API for my application, and obtain an API key.

I will store the key in an environment variable named `NYT_API_KEY` and access it in R using `Sys.getenv("NYT_API_KEY")`. The key will not appear in my Quarto document, GitHub repository, or published output.

## Planned Approach

I will use `httr2` to send the request and check whether it was successful. Then I will parse the JSON response and extract the article records into a data frame.

I plan to keep the article title, section, publication date, author byline, and URL. I will use `dplyr` to count the articles in each section and arrange the results from highest to lowest. A summary table and bar chart will show which sections appear most often in the returned list.

## Data-Cleaning Decisions

I will convert publication dates into R’s date format and check for missing or blank section names. Articles without a section will be labeled “Unknown” so they remain included in the counts.

The response may contain nested information, such as multimedia details. I will leave out fields that are not needed for my question and keep one row per article.

## Anticipated Challenges

The main challenges may be setting up the API key, handling request errors, and finding the article records within the JSON response. I will check the response before transforming it and avoid displaying my key in any output.

The most-viewed list changes over time, so running the same request on another day may produce different results. I will record when I retrieved the data to give the findings context.

## Expected Outcome

The final result will include a tidy article data frame, a table of article counts by section, and a bar chart. I will use these outputs to answer which sections are most represented in the seven-day most-viewed list. I will also explain that this is a snapshot of the returned articles and does not measure total readership.
